nutshell: Multi-modal object ReID (fusing RGB/NIR/TIR images) has no text annotations to exploit, and naive fusion of raw multi-modal features is noisy and computationally heavy. This paper (1) releases three new text-enhanced multi-modal ReID benchmarks by using an MLLM to generate and then structure per-modality captions into a fixed attribute template, and (2) proposes IDEA, combining an Inverted Multi-modal Feature Extractor (IMFE) that reverses text embeddings into pseudo-image tokens fed into the vision encoder (rather than the more common image-to-pseudo-text direction) with Cooperative Deformable Aggregation (CDA), which adaptively samples discriminative local regions shared across modalities and fuses them with global features via cross-attention.
contributions: Three new text-enhanced multi-modal object ReID benchmarks (built on RGBNT201, RGBNT100, MSVR310) via a two-step MLLM captioning pipeline: free-form caption generation per modality, then re-feeding the caption to the MLLM to extract predefined attributes into a fixed structured template, reducing caption redundancy/length variance.

Inverted Multi-modal Feature Extractor (IMFE): Modal Prefixes (learnable per-modality prompt tokens prepended to each modality's text) to reduce cross-modal text conflicts, plus an InverseNet that projects the text embedding into a pseudo-image token concatenated with patch tokens before the vision encoder - i.e. injecting semantic guidance into the image branch rather than the more typical reverse direction.

Cooperative Deformable Aggregation (CDA): a learned offset mechanism that adaptively samples discriminative local regions from a reference grid (offsets shared across modalities), then fuses the sampled local features with global (CLS + pseudo-token) features via cross-attention.

New SOTA mAP on all three benchmarks (RGBNT201: 80.2, RGBNT100: 87.2, MSVR310: 47.0), with ablations showing text, IMFE, and CDA each contribute a meaningful, fairly balanced share of the total gain over a no-text baseline (Table 3: 70.3 -> 73.4 -> 77.2 -> 80.2 mAP).
deficiencies: On RGBNT201 (Table 1), IDEA's own Rank-1 (82.1) is actually beaten by two of its listed CLIP-based competitors in the same table - MambaPro (83.4, bolded as best) and DeMo (82.3, underlined as second-best) - but the text only compares IDEA's Rank-1 gain against the weaker ViT-based TOP-ReID (76.6), never acknowledging it places third on Rank-1 among its own reported baselines.

Same selective framing on MSVR310 (Table 2): DeMo's mAP (49.2) is higher than IDEA's (47.0) in the very same table, yet the text only claims IDEA 'outperform[s] EDITOR by 8.0% mAP,' without noting it is actually second-best on mAP for this dataset, behind DeMo.

And on RGBNT100 (Table 2), DeMo's Rank-1 (97.6) and FACENet's Rank-1 (96.9) both beat IDEA's Rank-1 (96.5) - again unaddressed, with the narrative built entirely around IDEA's mAP win over EDITOR (82.1) rather than its closest actual competitor, DeMo.

Despite introducing three new MLLM-generated text-annotated benchmarks as a headline contribution, there is no quantitative validation of caption/attribute accuracy against ground truth (no human evaluation, no error rate reported) - the only evidence offered is a handful of qualitative example captions (Fig. 2), even though the paper's own InverseNet design is explicitly motivated by the expectation that 'generated texts may contain some errors and conflicts.'
notable: Every one of the strongest baselines IDEA compares against - TOP-ReID, EDITOR, MambaPro, and DeMo - shares overlapping authorship with this paper (Yuhao Wang and/or Pingping Zhang appear as authors on all four, with Huchuan Lu on most), meaning the primary SOTA comparisons are largely against the same research group's own prior work rather than independent competitors; useful context for weighing how the comparisons above should be read. Also notable: Fig. 4's prompt-length ablation surfaces a genuine architectural constraint - the learnable Modal-Prefix tokens share CLIP's fixed 77-token text budget with the actual generated caption, so a longer/more-informative prefix directly truncates the caption content, which is why the paper settles on a short prefix length (Np=2) despite otherwise finding that more prefix tokens 'boost model decisiveness.'
